entities.name: X-linked agammaglobulinemia
observations: Bruton disease is an X-linked primary antibody deficiency caused by impaired B-cell maturation.
Affected boys develop recurrent bacterial respiratory and ear infections after approximately 6 months, when transplacental maternal IgG declines.
The immunologic hallmark is profoundly reduced mature B cells and immunoglobulins, with absent or markedly reduced antibody production.

entities.name: BTK
observations: BTK encodes Bruton tyrosine kinase, required for B-cell development and maturation.
Pathogenic BTK variants cause X-linked agammaglobulinemia.

entities.name: XLA inheritance
observations: X-linked recessive inheritance explains affected male relatives through the maternal lineage; female carriers are generally clinically unaffected.
Most cases are inherited, while a minority arise from de novo pathogenic variants.

entities.name: Antibody deficiency prevalence
observations: Antibody deficiencies are the most common category of primary immunodeficiency and account for approximately half of reported primary immunodeficiencies in many classifications.

entities.name: Preoperative proteinuria
observations: Dipstick or UACR-measured proteinuria is independently associated with postoperative cardiac-surgery AKI across multiple adult cohorts.
Direct preserved-GFR evidence: in 1,246 adults with eGFR >60, proteinuria was associated with all AKI stages and dialysis-requiring AKI after adjustment.
In a prospective cohort with mean eGFR 96.3, heavy dipstick proteinuria was associated with AKI (adjusted OR 3.14, 95% CI 1.26–7.77).

entities.name: Postcardiotomy AKI
observations: In the direct preserved-GFR cohort, AKI occurred in 34.8% and renal replacement therapy was required in 2.9%; AKI was defined by AKIN criteria.
Proteinuria was associated with postoperative AKI in cardiac-surgery cohorts and in a cardiac-surgery meta-analysis.

entities.name: Proteinuria predicts AKI with preserved GFR
observations: A retrospective cohort restricted to eGFR >60 found preoperative dipstick proteinuria independently associated with all AKI stages and dialysis-requiring AKI after cardiac surgery.
The magnitude of association was not reported in the available abstract, so evidence supports prediction but does not quantify incremental discrimination in this subgroup.

entities.name: Proteinuria adds modest prediction
observations: Adding UACR to a clinical cardiac-surgery model increased AUC from 0.67 to 0.70 and produced 29% continuous net reclassification improvement.
The study did not isolate an eGFR >=60 subgroup, so incremental prediction specifically in preserved GFR remains less certain.

entities.name: Proteinuria meta-analysis
observations: A 2021 meta-analysis of 11 observational studies found preoperative proteinuria associated with postoperative AKI (adjusted OR 1.65, 95% CI 1.44–1.89); the cardiac-surgery subgroup adjusted OR was 1.69 (95% CI 1.39–2.06).
The pooled estimate was not restricted to eGFR >=60 and does not establish incremental discrimination beyond baseline renal function.
